questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: After a crash or when stopped for a traffic ticket.
Only when stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a crash or when stopped for a traffic ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. Show your insurance proof and license to a police officer when asked after a traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: You should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles have only one tail light, making them hard to see at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming.

questions.question: What should you do at a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection looks clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive fast through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Treat a broken traffic light as a four-way stop. Always stop completely and look both ways. Yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection, unless a police officer directs traffic.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid on water, you should quickly apply the brakes.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not slam on the brakes. Instead, ease off the gas pedal and try to regain control. Let the skid pass. Braking too hard will make it worse.

questions.question: How should you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and lights?

options.text: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to emergency vehicles with siren and lights on. Drive to the right edge and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When you see an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accidents just to look.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to use:

options.text: The full lane width like other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full lane width like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full width of a lane, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes in your direction. Many vehicles pass you on the right. What should you do?

options.text: Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to go fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the road for a long time without looking around.
Getting too much sleep before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for a long time without looking around.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and stop scanning ahead, beside, and behind you. You zone out and may not see traffic slowing or stopping in front of you, causing a crash.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop immediately and back up.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They tell you that work is being done on or next to the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before putting the car in reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Look in your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is risky because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Walk to the back of your car before backing to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol content (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects on your body.
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its harmful effects.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: When turning right, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you start to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before a right turn, move to the far right side of the road. Do not cut across lanes.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as regular driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, and others on the road at risk. Staying focused on driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to cars coming toward them. Wait until it is safe to turn.

questions.question: Increasing speed is the best way to avoid losing control in wet conditions.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can ride up on water and lose grip. This is called hydroplaning. Slow down when driving in wet conditions to avoid losing control.

questions.question: You do not need to follow a motorcycle as closely as you would follow a car.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry weather. Keep three to four seconds of distance behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to respond in an emergency.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular sign is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Let other cars and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left can then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They are not affected by speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances are longer and crashes are more severe when vehicles travel at higher speeds.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers have time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, where should you look?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left, right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from the left are closer to you than those from the right. Check across the entire intersection to make sure it is clear before you go.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, do not panic. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas to let the vehicle slow down. Apply the brakes lightly when it is safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed significantly.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter the circumstances. As a driver, you must stay alert to pedestrians and always yield to them, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through a flooded area. Even shallow-looking water can hide dangers. If you see flooding, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to an upcoming traffic signal. Be ready for red, yellow, and green lights, and watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey first?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all signs, signals, and road markings. Traffic officers include police, fire police, road work flag persons, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed?

options.text: After coming to a complete stop first.
If you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane, regardless of other signals. Always yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection before turning.
